wallHeight.Name: Wall height (ft)
wallHeight.Hint: How tall sight-blocking walls are in the 3D view.

doorHeight.Name: Door height (ft)
doorHeight.Hint: How tall closed doors are in the 3D view.

raiseDark.Name: Raise dark areas as rock
raiseDark.Hint: Very dark parts of the map (black rock, out-of-bounds) become solid rock pillars and walls. Turn this off for night maps with dark floors.

rockHeight.Name: Rock height (ft above the floor)
rockHeight.Hint: How tall the rock made from dark areas is.

darkThreshold.Name: How dark counts as rock
darkThreshold.Hint: Brightness from 0 to 255. Higher = more of the map becomes rock.

trimColor.Name: Glow trim colour
trimColor.Hint: The glowing strip along the top of walls and platform edges (hex colour).

wallSkin.Name: Wall skin
wallSkin.Hint: What walls and doors are made of in the 3D view, to fit your maps. Raised areas are built of it too for natural materials (stone, wood, marble...); sci-fi skins keep them plain metal. Each scene can pick its own in Scene Config > Vantage.

mood.Name: Lighting mood
mood.Hint: The light of the 3D view. Automatic keeps the light painted on the map. A mood tints it and adds a sun or moon (with shadows when Shadows is Full), its sky, haze and glow. Each scene can pick its own in Scene Config > Vantage.

lightColor.Name: Light colour
lightColor.Hint: Recolour the sun or moon, the sky and the haze (for example purple for a fey realm, red for a vampire's blood moon). Works with every mood; with Automatic it switches to the Custom colour mood. Empty = each mood's own colours. Each scene can pick its own in Scene Config > Vantage.

bloom.Name: Glow (bloom)
bloom.Hint: Bright lights and trims bleed a soft glow.

snapshotWidth.Name: Snapshot width (px)
snapshotWidth.Hint: Size of the picture sent with Show Players.

standeeArt.Name: Figure pictures
standeeArt.Hint: Which picture stands up as each token's figure. Portrait = the actor's upright art (best when your tokens are top-down; otherwise figures look like they lean toward you). While a token wears another form (for example a Visage transformation), the Tokenizer ".Avatar." twin of its image is used. Token image = the token art itself.

Choices.tilt: Token image, leaning back (top-down token art)

tiltDeg.Name: Leaning figures: angle
tiltDeg.Hint: How far "leaning back" figures tilt, in degrees. Match it to how high above the character the token art was drawn: about 30-45 for high-angle tokens, 60-70 for straight-down ones.

heightMapMax.Name: Height maps: tallest point (ft)
heightMapMax.Hint: If a map image has a grey height map next to it named <map name>_height.webp (or .png / .jpg), white parts rise this many feet above the floor and black stays flat. 0 = off.

playersCanOpen.Name: Players can open the 3D view
playersCanOpen.Hint: Lets players open it from their own tokens. It shows only tokens they can see (and, with the next setting, only what their tokens can see).

playersVision.Name: Players' 3D views follow their sight
playersVision.Hint: On = in Live views (and the window, if players can open it) players see only what their tokens see right now; places they explored before stay dim grey; the rest is dark, like fog of war on the map. Show Players pictures are never limited (you choose what to send). Off = players see everything you show.

shadows.Name: Shadows + corner shading
shadows.Hint: Full = the 4 nearest lights cast shadows from walls, rock and raised areas, plus soft shading in corners. Corner shading only is lighter on slow computers.

blurMoving.Name: Lower resolution while moving
blurMoving.Hint: On = the picture drops to half resolution while you drag or walk the camera, so it stays smooth on slow computers (it looks slightly blurry while moving). Off = always sharp.

animate.Name: Animate the 3D view
animate.Hint: On = video maps play, animated lights flicker and pulse, and weather moves (about 30 frames a second while anything moves). Off = a still picture, lighter on slow computers.

sound3d.Name: 3D sound
sound3d.Hint: While the 3D view is open on the scene you're on, its ambient sounds are heard from the camera (louder as you walk toward them, with Foundry's walls and muffling) and panned left and right by where they are around you.

Region.Hint: Raises this area into a solid block in the 3D view: a crate, console, counter or dais (the map art stays on top). Negative = a pit. Leave empty for a normal region. Tokens inside stand on top.
Region.UnderHint: Empty = a solid block. A number below the Height makes it float: a bridge deck (Height 10, Underside 9), a balcony, a roof or an awning, with room to walk and see under it. Tokens at its height stand on top.
Region.LookHint: With a height: what the sides of this block look like (the top keeps the map art). The front faces the open floor unless you pick a side.
Region.PicHint: Optional: an image (a cabinet front, a shop sign, a door) drawn on the front face, top to bottom. Transparent parts show the look underneath.
Region.SkinHint: Walls (and raised areas) inside this region wear this skin: a brick building on a neon street, a wooden cabin in a stone keep. It works with or without a height.

Token.FigureHint: Standing = an upright cut-out (best for side-view or full-body art). Leaning back = for top-down token art, so it doesn't look like it tips toward you. Set it on the actor's Prototype Token to change every copy.
Token.PictureHint: A different picture just for the 3D view (for example full-body art with a transparent background). Empty = automatic.

Window.ShowPlayersTitle: Send this picture to every player
Window.LiveTitle: Players' screens follow your camera live
Window.RebuildTitle: Rebuild from the scene (walls, levels, lights, tokens)
Window.Help: Drag: look · WASD: move · Q/E: down/up (Overview: turn) · Wheel: zoom · Shift: fast · Double-click: walk there · Click: door / pick a token · Right-click: target
Window.TimeTitle: Time of day: drag from noon to night. Sets the scene's darkness and the Day cycle lighting mood.
Window.FilmTitle: Cutscenes and clips: camera points, play, record a video

Notify.GMOnly: Vantage: only the GM can open the 3D view.
Notify.LiveOn: Vantage: players now follow your camera. Click Live again to stop.
Notify.DayCycle: Vantage: this scene's lighting mood is now Day cycle, so the 3D light follows the time of day.
Notify.PickToken: Vantage: pick a token first (click its figure, or choose whose eyes).
Notify.NotYours: Vantage: you can only move your own tokens.
Notify.Blocked: Vantage: a wall is in the way.
Notify.TargetScene: Vantage: targeting works on the scene that is open on the map.
Notify.NeedPoints: Vantage: add at least 2 camera points first (move the camera, click Add point, move, Add point...).

Scene.HeightMaxHint: How tall the white parts of this scene's height map are. Empty = the world setting.
Scene.RaiseDarkHint: Override the world setting for this scene (handy for night maps with dark floors).
Scene.WallSkinHint: What this scene's walls are made of. Empty = the world setting.
Scene.MoodHint: The light of this scene in 3D: a sun, moon or night glow to match the map's vibe. Empty = the world setting.
Scene.SunAzHint: Where the sun or moon stands, as a compass bearing: 0 = top of the map, 90 = right, 180 = bottom, 270 = left. Match the shadows painted on the map. Empty = the mood's own.
Scene.LightColorHint: Tints the sun or moon, the sky and the haze: purple for a fey realm, red for a blood moon, green for a swamp. Empty = the world setting (or the mood's own colours).
Scene.WeatherHint: Rain, snow, fog and more in 3D. Empty = whatever the scene shows in Foundry (its weather, or FXMaster's). Regions with a Suppress Weather behaviour stay dry, and so does everything under a higher level.

Film.Title: Cutscene
Film.AddTitle: Add where the camera is now as the next point of the path (saved with the scene)
Film.PlayTitle: Fly the camera along the points (players in Live see it too)
Film.RecordTitle: Record a video of the window (with 2+ points: records the cutscene; without: until you click again)

Prep.Title: Prep this map for 3D
Prep.Hint: One click: hills that rise from the map's water (rivers, shores), raised areas from the scene's tiles (crates, tables, cars... with a look from their names; bridges and roofs float), and looks for raised regions from their names. You see what it found first; everything it makes can be undone.
Prep.Intro: Here is what Vantage found on this scene. Tick what to do:
Prep.WaterFound: About {pct}% of the map looks like water (cyan in the picture below): the ground rises away from it, up to the scene's height-map height (8 ft if not set). Untick it if the cyan isn't water.
Prep.WaterNone: No water found on the map art.
Prep.TilesNone: No tiles that look like objects.
Prep.LooksFound: {n} raised regions get a look from their names.
Prep.LooksNone: No raised regions without a look whose names give one away.
Prep.UndoHint: {n} things from an earlier prep are on this scene (Undo removes them).
Prep.Done: Vantage: map prepped. Height map from the water: {water}; {tiles} raised areas from tiles; {looks} looks set.
Prep.Undone: Vantage: removed {n} regions from the earlier prep, and its height map.
